question: For weighted geometric compositions of conditional diffusion distributions, when does failure come from using the wrong intermediate-time score path, when does it come from learned-score extrapolation, and can Feynman-Kac particle correction repair either source of error?

key_findings.claim: A weighted Gaussian product is not automatically a probability distribution when weights can be negative.
key_findings.evidence: For zero-mean Gaussians, Theorem 1 proves that the product is normalizable exactly when the weighted precision sum is positive definite, in which case the target covariance is its inverse. This is a validity condition on the target, not a sampling result.

key_findings.claim: Even exact source scores need not make naive linear score composition sample the intended product distribution.
key_findings.evidence: For zero-mean Gaussians with mutually commuting covariances and weights summing to one, Theorem 2 derives the naive probability-flow ODE covariance as the weighted matrix-geometric product of source covariances, whereas the target covariance is the inverse weighted precision sum. With covariances epsilon I and epsilon^-1 I at equal weights, their operator-norm ratio diverges as epsilon approaches zero.

anchors.section: Appendix D.2, integration and boundary conditions

key_findings.claim: The Gaussian mismatch theorem is narrow: it characterizes the naive denoising ODE, not every sampler or every Gaussian family.
key_findings.evidence: The proof requires zero means, positive-definite pairwise-commuting covariances, scalar isotropic noising, a standard-normal terminal distribution, and weights summing to one. It does not establish the same closed form for noncommuting covariances, nonzero means, the stochastic reverse SDE, or a corrected sampler.

anchors.section: Appendix D.2, commutativity and covariance evolution

key_findings.claim: Base composition has a causal-intervention motivation only when perturbations change disjoint mechanisms under an invertible latent representation.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix B derives P_double = P_a P_b / P_0 by assuming an observational causal model, a diffeomorphic feature map, and independent interventions with non-overlapping targets. The empirical room mixtures are motivated by this derivation but are not shown to satisfy its latent causal assumptions.

anchors.section: Appendix B, perturbations and weighted composition

key_findings.claim: Under exact factorized conditionals and coordinate-wise isotropic noising, Feynman-Kac correction has zero log-weight drift and coincides with the naive denoising SDE.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 3 uses disjoint coordinate blocks and base weights to cancel the divergence and squared-score terms. Lemma 2 preserves block factorization under coordinate-wise noising, and Corollary 3.1 gives uniform particle weights throughout the exact-score trajectory.

key_findings.claim: The proof shows that learned-score error drives a nonzero FKC residual, but it does not prove that FKC must move farther from the target under every learned error.
key_findings.evidence: The post-Theorem-3 remark asserts that resampling concentrates on noise and consequently drifts farther, yet the theorem and proof cover exact scores only. No sign condition, distance monotonicity theorem, or global learned-error bound establishes the stronger consequence; it is supported empirically in selected OOD settings.

key_findings.claim: The synthetic design usefully crosses factorization, target support, score oracle status, training-set size, and particle count.
key_findings.evidence: The experiments vary ID versus OOD targets, factorized versus non-factorized source distributions, analytic versus learned scores, N in {100, 1,000, 10,000}, and K in {1, 4, 16, 64, 256}; each table uses 5,000 target and generated samples over 30 runs.

anchors.section: Appendix F.1, training, sampling, metrics, and seeds

key_findings.claim: Factorized ID Gaussians provide a negative control: exact FKC has no benefit, and extra particles can amplify error in an undertrained learned model.
key_findings.evidence: Analytic SW2 stays between 0.0346 and 0.0376 across K, consistent with zero exact correction. At N = 100, learned SW2 worsens from 0.3537 at K = 1 to 0.5261 at K = 256 and MMD2 rises from 0.0252 to 0.0684.

key_findings.claim: Non-factorized ID Gaussians show correction only when score estimation is sufficiently accurate.
key_findings.evidence: With analytic scores, SW2 improves from 0.0655 at K = 1 to 0.0333 at K = 256. With N = 100, it instead worsens from 0.4454 to 0.6216; with N = 10,000 it improves modestly to 0.0740 at K = 64 before rising to 0.0793 at K = 256.

key_findings.claim: Factorized OOD Gaussians isolate score-estimation failure: analytic FKC remains neutral while learned FKC deteriorates sharply with K.
key_findings.evidence: Analytic SW2 remains about 0.112-0.114. For N = 10,000, learned SW2 rises from 0.3948 at K = 1 to 2.8210 at K = 256, and MMD2 rises from 0.0025 to 0.1269.

key_findings.claim: In non-factorized OOD Gaussians, exact correction is strong but learned correction moves in the opposite direction.
key_findings.evidence: Analytic SW2 falls from 0.6375 at K = 1 to 0.0820 at K = 256 and analytic MMD2 approaches zero. At N = 10,000, SW2 rises from 0.8518 to 2.8322 and MMD2 from 0.0172 to 0.1455, directly exhibiting the approximation-error versus estimation-error tradeoff.

key_findings.claim: Gaussian-mixture experiments reproduce non-monotone learned OOD correction but also show that even the analytic finite-particle sampler remains imperfect.
key_findings.evidence: For ID GMMs, analytic SW2 drops from 1.2133 at K = 1 to 0.0736 at K = 64. For OOD GMMs, N = 10,000 improves from 3.9606 to 2.1718 at K = 16 then worsens to 2.6706 at K = 256, while analytic SW2 still equals 1.4670 at K = 256 rather than reaching the reference distribution.

key_findings.claim: Separate expert networks usually compose worse than a shared conditional network, but the stated weight-sharing explanation is suggestive rather than identified and has an OOD-GMM exception.
key_findings.evidence: For factorized OOD Gaussians at N = 10,000 and K = 256, separate-expert SW2 is 4.7380 versus 2.8210 for the shared model. Conversely, in OOD GMMs the separate model reaches 1.3582 versus 2.6706 at the same N and K. Parameter sharing, optimization, and model allocation all change together.

key_findings.claim: The room study is qualitative and does not causally identify factorization or cleanly hold the target combination out of all source distributions.
key_findings.evidence: Painting versus coffee table changes identity, position, occlusion, and source-generator difficulty along with the locality proxy. The OOD base mixture explicitly assigns beta = 0.05/3, about 1.67%, to the couch-plus-X class, while exact numerical OOD weights for P_a1 and P_a2 are not reported. Figures 2 and 4 show selected grids without a quantitative scorer, uncertainty, or sampling-selection protocol.

anchors.section: Section 5.3, OOD mixture description and Figure 2

key_findings.claim: Numerical and compute choices complicate interpretation of the particle-count curves.
key_findings.evidence: Synthetic FKC clips each log-weight-drift increment to [-15, 15], uses 500 integration steps, and scales swarm work with K. Appendix C also notes that FKC resampling for deterministic ODE trajectories duplicates identical paths and monotonically reduces diversity; the experiments instead center the stochastic sampler, so ODE theory and SDE empirics should not be conflated.

key_findings.claim: The headline infeasibility statement is a conjecture, not a lower bound over inference-time algorithms.
key_findings.evidence: The abstract explicitly says the authors conjecture that no inference-time technique can efficiently sample certain targets. The formal results cover a naive Gaussian ODE and an exact factorized FKC special case; experiments cover naive composition and one clipped FKC implementation, without a complexity lower bound or matched-budget comparison to other correctors.

method.core_idea: Decompose compositional sampling error into an intermediate-time approximation term and a learned-score estimation term, then manipulate each term with analytic scores, support shift, factorization, and Feynman-Kac particle count.
method.mechanism: Weighted geometric products define target distributions. Naive sampling linearly combines source scores even though noising and composition need not commute. FKC tracks a proxy weighted composition of noised marginals with sequentially reweighted particles; exact factorization can cancel its correction, whereas learned errors can dominate the particle weights in low-support regions.
assumptions: All source distributions have mutually equivalent positive densities with respect to a common base measure, and the weighted product has a finite positive normalizer.
Theorem 1 uses zero-mean positive-definite Gaussians; Theorem 2 additionally requires pairwise-commuting covariances and weights summing to one.
Theorem 3 uses base-composition weights, disjoint coordinate blocks, exact scores, and scalar coordinate-wise isotropic noising.
The causal interpretation assumes an invertible latent representation and perturbations with non-overlapping intervention targets.
ID and OOD are operationalized by effective source support in hand-designed distributions rather than by a universal formal threshold.
Synthetic metrics rely on exact Gaussian targets, exact ID-GMM rejection sampling, or an asymptotically approximate OOD-GMM importance reference.
The room study assumes wall/floor spatial separation is a proxy for probabilistic factorization and that FLUX generation plus DINOv2 filtering yields comparable image pools.
The implemented clipped, discretized FKC sampler adequately represents the ideal continuous-time corrector for the tested conclusions.

techniques.role: Defines products, quotients, and base compositions of source distributions.
Linearly combines conditional scores and supplies the inference-mismatch baseline.
Uses weighted particles and systematic resampling to correct a noised-composition path.
Removes neural score error while factorization and target support are varied.
Crosses N and K to expose non-monotone interactions between estimation and correction.
Measures two-dimensional sample mismatch across 30 independent runs.
Tests whether conditional weight sharing correlates with compositional accuracy.
Builds filtered object-combination image classes for a qualitative higher-dimensional demonstration.

evaluations.setting: Factorized ID 2D Gaussians; N in {100, 1,000, 10,000}, analytic scores, K in {1, 4, 16, 64, 256}; 30 runs and 5,000 samples (Table 1a; Appendix H.1).
evaluations.metric: Sliced Wasserstein-2 and unbiased RBF MMD2 against 5,000 exact target samples.
evaluations.result: Analytic SW2 remains 0.0346-0.0376. At N = 100, learned SW2 worsens 0.3537 to 0.5261 and MMD2 0.0252 to 0.0684 from K = 1 to 256.
evaluations.baseline: Naive K = 1; exact-score behavior is the theorem-aligned no-correction control.

evaluations.setting: Non-factorized ID 2D Gaussians under the same sweep (Table 1b; Appendix H.1).
evaluations.metric: SW2 and MMD2, mean +/- standard deviation over 30 runs.
evaluations.result: Analytic SW2 improves 0.0655 to 0.0333 by K = 256; N = 100 worsens 0.4454 to 0.6216, while N = 10,000 reaches 0.0740 at K = 64 versus 0.0957 at K = 1.
evaluations.baseline: Naive K = 1, separating correctable path mismatch from learned-score error.

evaluations.setting: Factorized OOD 2D Gaussians under the same sweep (Table 1c; Appendix H.1).
evaluations.metric: SW2 and MMD2 against the exact N(0,10I) target.
evaluations.result: Analytic SW2 remains about 0.112-0.114. At N = 10,000, SW2 worsens 0.3948 to 2.8210 and MMD2 0.0025 to 0.1269 from K = 1 to 256.
evaluations.baseline: Exact-score neutral correction and learned naive K = 1.

evaluations.setting: Non-factorized OOD 2D Gaussians under the same sweep (Table 1d; Appendix H.1).
evaluations.metric: SW2 and MMD2 against the exact target.
evaluations.result: Analytic SW2 improves 0.6375 to 0.0820 and MMD2 approaches zero; N = 10,000 instead worsens from 0.8518 to 2.8322 SW2 and 0.0172 to 0.1455 MMD2.
evaluations.baseline: Naive K = 1, showing opposite K trends for oracle and learned scores.

evaluations.setting: Non-factorized ID and OOD 2D Gaussian mixtures (Table 2; Appendix H.3).
evaluations.metric: SW2 and MMD2 against exact rejection-sampled ID or 1,000-times-oversampled importance-sampled OOD references.
evaluations.result: ID analytic SW2 improves 1.2133 to 0.0736 at K = 64. OOD N = 10,000 improves 3.9606 to 2.1718 at K = 16 then worsens to 2.6706; analytic reaches 1.4670 at K = 256.
evaluations.baseline: Naive K = 1; OOD reference error and finite-particle error prevent interpreting small differences as exact sampler bias.

evaluations.setting: Separate score experts versus one shared conditional score network (Appendix E; H.2; H.4).
evaluations.result: Separate experts are generally worse, including factorized OOD N = 10,000, K = 256 SW2 of 4.7380 versus 2.8210; the exception is OOD GMM at the same N,K, where separate experts reach 1.3582 versus 2.6706.
evaluations.baseline: Shared conditional network; parameterization and optimization change with sharing, so this is not an isolated regularization intervention.

evaluations.setting: 256x256 FLUX-generated rooms with couch-plus-painting and couch-plus-coffee-table mixtures, K = 1 versus K = 16 (Section 5.3; Figures 2 and 4).
evaluations.metric: Visual inspection of displayed sample grids only.
evaluations.result: Displayed ID grids improve with K = 16, factorized-proxy OOD grids remain similar or more warped, and non-factorized OOD grids fail to show reliable simultaneous objects. No numerical rate, blind rating, random-grid rule, seed count, or uncertainty is reported.
evaluations.baseline: Naive K = 1; object identity and support overlap change together, and the base OOD source retains about 1.67% target-class mass.

evaluations.setting: Compute, architecture, and reproducibility audit (Appendix F).
evaluations.metric: Reported model, data, hardware, training, and sampling specifications.
evaluations.result: Synthetic models are four-layer width-512 MLPs trained 20,000 iterations and sampled with 500 steps; each table costs about seven GPU-hours. Image models use a four-level conditional U-Net, 50 epochs, batch 16, 100 inference steps, and about nine hours on one L40S/A6000-class GPU.
evaluations.baseline: No matched score-evaluation or wall-clock comparison across K, no large pretrained diffusion baseline, and no architecture or domain replication.

limitations: Author-stated: experiments cover only vanilla conditional diffusion models and require validation before extending to other conditional generators.
Author-stated: experiments study only base-composed weights, not general weighted compositions.
Author-stated: theory is highly specialized to an analytically solvable toy Gaussian setting and leaves general score-error behavior open.
Reviewer-identified: the broad efficient-inference impossibility is conjectural and is not a complexity lower bound over all correctors.
Reviewer-identified: the image study does not hold the target class out of every source distribution, omits exact OOD conditional mixture vectors, and provides no duplicate/leakage audit.
Reviewer-identified: painting versus coffee table confounds factorization with identity, placement, occlusion, prompt adherence, and filtering difficulty.
Reviewer-identified: image evidence is selected and qualitative, without a prespecified metric, test split, seed analysis, uncertainty, or blinded sampling rule.
Reviewer-identified: increasing K increases score-network work and memory; no wall-clock- or network-evaluation-matched corrector comparison is made.
Reviewer-identified: synthetic log-weight increments are clipped at 15, whereas exact continuous-time statements concern the ideal residual.
Reviewer-identified: the OOD GMM reference is asymptotic importance sampling, not an exact independent oracle.
Reviewer-identified: the proof that learned error makes the residual nonzero does not imply monotonic degradation for arbitrary errors.
Reviewer-identified: evidence stops at 2D densities and one modest class-conditional U-Net; latent diffusion, flow matching, and large text-to-image transfer are untested.
failure_modes: Noising and geometric composition can fail to commute, so exact linear score addition follows the wrong intermediate path.
Learned source scores can be queried in low-density target regions and return unconstrained extrapolations.
Particle reweighting can preferentially replicate score errors, causing larger K to degrade rather than improve samples.
Systematic resampling can lose diversity; for deterministic ODE paths, duplicated particles remain identical thereafter.
Weight clipping can suppress degeneracy but also truncate the correction needed for exact-score path mismatch.
Rare target-class exposure can masquerade as zero-shot compositional extrapolation.
A visual locality proxy can fail because lighting, perspective, occlusion, and generator semantics couple nominally separate regions.
Approximate target samples or selected qualitative grids can overstate small and unstable gains.
Separate expert networks can lose the shared model's implicit cross-condition regularization, although this is not universal.
reusable_insights: Cross exact versus learned scores before attributing compositional failure to either the sampler or the score model.
Use factorized distributions as a no-correction control and coupled Gaussians as an analytically falsifiable correction control.
Report target-combination mass in every source; rare exposure and an absent combination are distinct regimes.
Plot quality against score-network evaluations and wall-clock in addition to particle count.
A corrector can amplify model error even when it is mathematically exact with oracle scores, so score uncertainty should inform resampling.
To test a factorization mechanism causally, vary dependency structure while holding object identity, rendering, and support fixed.
Separate theorem scope for probability-flow ODEs from stochastic reverse-SDE and finite-particle implementations.
open_questions: Can any inference-time method achieve calibrated error bounds when all learned source scores are unconstrained on target-support regions?
Can score uncertainty or effective sample size predict when increasing K will amplify rather than repair error?
How do DriftLite, MCMC, distilled-energy SMC, and other correctors compare at matched score evaluations and wall-clock?
Does an explicitly local, object-centric, or causal score architecture extrapolate when the composite class is truly absent from every source?
Can the Gaussian mismatch theorem be generalized to noncommuting covariances, nonzero means, stochastic reverse SDEs, or nonlinear scores?
What finite-sample guarantees apply to the OOD importance-reference sampler and the clipped FKC implementation?
Can a quantitative natural-image benchmark manipulate factorization independently of object identity and prompt difficulty?
Do the error decomposition and non-monotone particle effects persist in latent diffusion, flow matching, and large pretrained generators?

competitive_landscape.title: Mechanisms of Projective Composition of Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Bradley et al. define projective composition, characterize exact and failing linear-score regimes, and introduce the factorized-conditional framework. The present paper adds an explicit learned-score-error axis and the FKC zero-residual corollary.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v3, updated 2025-09-25T20:57:40Z; official arXiv Atom record verified 2026-08-23

competitive_landscape.title: Feynman-Kac Correctors in Diffusion: Annealing, Guidance, and Product of Experts
competitive_landscape.difference: Skreta et al. introduce the particle corrector used here for annealed, guided, and product distributions. The present paper stress-tests that method with exact-versus-learned scores and derives a factorized case where its correction vanishes.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v2, updated 2025-06-08T05:40:55Z; official arXiv Atom record verified 2026-08-23

competitive_landscape.title: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle: Compositional Generation with Energy-Based Diffusion Models and MCMC
competitive_landscape.difference: Du et al. attribute many composition failures to sampling and use energy parameterization plus MCMC, including Metropolis-corrected variants. Those samplers are an important unmatched comparator to the present broader inference-time conjecture.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v6, updated 2024-09-14T18:55:50Z; official arXiv Atom record verified 2026-08-23

competitive_landscape.title: DriftLite: Lightweight Drift Control for Inference-Time Scaling of Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: DriftLite moves part of the Feynman-Kac potential into an on-the-fly control drift to reduce weight variance and reports guidance/SMC comparisons. It directly challenges claims about particle degeneracy and efficiency but is not evaluated at matched budget here.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v2, updated 2026-02-21T23:49:02Z; official arXiv Atom record verified 2026-08-23; ICLR 2026 conference version

competitive_landscape.title: Local Mechanisms of Compositional Generalization in Conditional Diffusion
competitive_landscape.difference: Bradley proves an equivalence between conditional projective composition and local conditional scores, then causally restores CLEVR length generalization by enforcing locality. This provides cleaner mechanism evidence than changing paintings to tables, while targeting a different compositional axis.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v3, updated 2026-03-13T00:01:09Z; official arXiv Atom record verified 2026-08-23

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Visual Generation with Composable Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Liu et al. introduced energy/product-based visual score composition for novel concept combinations. The present work explains an intermediate-time mismatch and demonstrates how learned target-support error can dominate it.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v6, updated 2023-01-17T17:08:51Z; official arXiv Atom record verified 2026-08-23

competitive_landscape.title: Composition and Control with Distilled Energy Diffusion Models and Sequential Monte Carlo
competitive_landscape.difference: Thornton et al. distill a pretrained score into an energy and use that energy as an SMC potential for composition and low-temperature sampling. It changes training representation rather than relying on vanilla learned scores at unsupported targets.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v1, updated 2025-02-18T11:47:44Z; official arXiv Atom record verified 2026-08-23; AISTATS 2025 version

competitive_landscape.title: Test-Time Compositional Generalization in Diffusion Models via Concept Discovery
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang et al. discover query-specific density modes from time-indexed scores, build an analytic product-of-experts teacher, and evaluate held-out ColorMNIST and CelebA compositions. Its query and optional adaptation assumptions differ from fixed base composition, but it is direct counterevidence to an unqualified inference-time impossibility framing.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v1, updated 2026-05-08T00:53:53Z; official arXiv Atom record verified 2026-08-23

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a unified theory-guided decomposition of catastrophic compositional generation, argues that learned OOD score error can dominate inference mismatch, and conjectures that no efficient inference-time technique can solve some vanilla-model compositions.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The strongest evidence is the exact-score/learned-score factorial design: four Gaussian regimes, two GMM regimes, N-by-K sweeps over 30 runs, and exact factorized cancellation. Theorem 2 formalizes one naive-ODE mismatch and Theorem 3 formalizes an exact FKC no-benefit case. Natural-image support is qualitative and confounded, and no lower bound covers general correctors.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the controlled empirical separation of inference-path and learned-score errors, together with the factorized FKC cancellation result and unusually clear negative particle-count curves. Projective composition, FKC, MCMC/energy correction, drift control, locality-based mechanisms, and test-time concept composition all predate the paper, so the evidence supports a warning about vanilla learned scores in low-support regions rather than a general impossibility of inference-time composition.

reviewer_notes: Secondary verification read all 41 pages of the exact pinned PDF, including the full reference list, Appendices A-C, every line of the three proofs in Appendix D, separate-expert Appendix E, all implementation and data details in Appendix F, rendered image grids in Figures 2 and 4, and all 27 supplemental tables. Primary-pass repairs include changing theory anchors from Section 3 to Section 4, experiments from Section 4 to Section 5, discussion from Section 5 to Section 6, dataset details from Appendix G to F.3, and removing a duplicated source_version key. The audit also corrected the prior statement 'beta/3': the paper sets beta = 0.05/3 and explicitly gives that mass in P0, while omitting exact numerical OOD vectors for the two perturbation distributions. Theorem scope, ideal-versus-clipped implementation, stochastic-versus-ODE sampling, approximate OOD ground truth, shared-expert confounding, and qualitative image selection are kept separate from author conclusions.

verification.passage_check: Independently checked the exact 41-page pinned PDF and text end to end. Verified the density assumption; Equations 1-11; Theorems 1-3, Lemmas 1-2 and Corollary 3.1 against their proofs; the ODE-resampling caveat; every Table 1-3 value used in findings; all SW2 and MMD2 expansions in Tables 4-27; 30-run/5,000-sample/2,000-projection protocols; clipping 15; 500 synthetic and 100 image steps; OOD importance oversampling 1000x; all U-Net/data/filtering/compute details; and both rendered room-image figures. Corrected all stale sections and identified where a learned-error remark and broad infeasibility conjecture exceed proved results.
verification.competitor_check: Re-searched official primary literature with mechanism/task, evaluation/baseline, and novelty-language query families. Verified 8 direct exact-version arXiv records by canonical ID, exact title, abstract, version URL, and update timestamp through 2026-08-23: projective-composition theory, FKC, energy-MCMC, DriftLite, locality mechanisms, composable diffusion, distilled-energy SMC, and test-time concept discovery. The last record was missing from the primary landscape and materially narrows an unqualified inference-time impossibility claim.
